summary: Confirmed and empirically reproduced the check_undeclared_scripts() bug: find-based enumeration flags gitignored __pycache__/*.pyc under literature/scripts/. Verified the fix (git ls-files, matching _git_deployed_files' existing pattern) requires re-deriving the prefix-strip against REPO_ROOT-relative form, since git ls-files output shape differs from find's absolute-path output. Simulated the exact fix across all extensions: only literature differs, removing precisely the 2 known-bad entries with zero regressions elsewhere.
decisions_made: Enumeration: git -C "$REPO_ROOT" ls-files "$ext_path_norm/scripts" replaces find "$ext_path_norm/scripts" -type f, mirroring _git_deployed_files' already-chosen pattern

Prefix-strip must be re-derived: introduce ext_rel="${ext_path_norm#"$REPO_ROOT"/}" and strip rel_path against ext_rel/scripts/, not the absolute ext_path_norm, because git ls-files always returns REPO_ROOT-relative paths regardless of pathspec form
Existence guard changes from [[ -f "$script_file" ]] to [[ -f "$REPO_ROOT/$script_file" ]] since script_file is now REPO_ROOT-relative, matching check_flat_category_orphans' analogous pattern
All other behavior preserved unchanged: full relative-path matching, no *.sh glob restriction, deprecated/* exemption, tests/ non-exemption, trailing-slash normalization of ext_path
